newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Rexrodt to remain minister, party says.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Rexrodt to remain minister, party says.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt has no plans to leave office, a leader of his Free Democrat party (FDP) said on Tuesday.

FDP general secretary Guido Westerwelle dismissed as "an empty rumour" a report due to be published in Stern magazine this week which said party leaders had agreed Rexrodt should step down after Easter.
"The FDP wants to continue its successful work with Rexrodt in the cabinet," Westerwelle said in a statement.
Rexrodt has come under regular file over his handling of the economy portfolio, which has been run by the FDP since Chancellor Helmut Kohl's formed his centre-right coalition government in 1982.

The FDP's Bonn headquarters was besieged last week by miners protesting over cuts in coal subsidies, an area for which Rexrodt is responsible. He had argued strongly for the cuts despite the thousands of job losses which would result.

Stern said the FDP's chairman in North Rhine-Westphalia Juergen Moellemann -- a former economics minister -- had called for party leader Wolfgang Gerhardt to join the cabinet. But FDP spokesman Rolf Goebel said Gerhardt had no ambitions to become a minister during parliament's current term ending in 1998.
